$comment: Every path this plugin delivers, and who owns it. Anything NOT listed here is the project's and is never touched. The update only ever touches a file the plugin actually changed between the installed and the target version.

classes.project: Created from a template once, then handed to the project. An update never rewrites it; when the upstream template changed, the update SUGGESTS how to fold that change in and lets the project decide. In practice these are rarely touched.
classes.plugin: Belongs to the plugin and is replaced on update. `project-specific: <id>` marker blocks inside such a file protect project content across the replacement.
classes.mixed: A plugin file where markers cannot work — the project's content and the plugin's are interleaved, or the format carries no comments. Claude merges these by hand, every time, always showing the diff.

entries.note: Only the library files matched at init are installed; a newly shipped one is offered, never forced.
Plugin-owned. A project adds its own hook as a new file — manifest-driven mirroring leaves it alone, and its settings.json entry survives because that merge only ever adds.

rules: Before creating a new file, check whether the project already has one by that name; if so, resolve it explicitly instead of overwriting.
Only files whose plugin version actually changed between the installed and target release are touched at all.
Mirroring a plugin directory refreshes the listed files and deletes what a previous manifest listed and this one no longer does — anything else in that directory belongs to the project and stays.
Removing or moving a file: inspect what project content it holds first and resolve that case specifically. Never delete a path without accounting for the project's share of it.
